02
Q 29:1–3 · Vol. 3, pp. 438–440

Verses 1 to 3

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Alif-Lam-Mim (1) Do the people think that they will be left to say "We believe" while they are not tried? (2) We certainly tried those before them, and God will surely know those who are truthful, and He will surely know the liars (3)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الم (1) أَحَسِبَ النَّاسُ أَنْ يُتْرَكُوا أَنْ يَقُولُوا آمَنَّا وَهُمْ لا يُفْتَنُونَ (2) وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْكاذِبِينَ (3)
Vol. 3, p. 438
The verb of reckoning (ḥasiba) cannot properly be attached to the meanings of single words, but only to the contents of whole sentences. Do you not see that if you said "I reckoned Zayd" or "I supposed the horse," it would amount to nothing until you said "I reckoned Zayd to be learned" or "I supposed the horse to be a thoroughbred"? For your saying "Zayd is learned" or "the horse is a thoroughbred" is speech that indicates a content, and you wanted to report that content as established in your mind by way of conjecture, not certainty. So you could find no alternative, in expressing its being established in your mind in that manner, but to mention both halves of the sentence and bring the verb of reckoning in over them, so that your purpose is complete.
الحسبان لا يصح تعليقه بمعاني المفردات، ولكن بمضامين الجمل. ألا ترى أنك لو قلت: حسبت زيدا وظننت الفرس: لم يكن شيئا حتى تقول: حسبت زيدا عالما وظننت الفرس جوادا، لأنّ قولك: زيد عالم، أو الفرس جواد كلام دال على مضمون، فأردت الإخبار عن ذلك المضمون ثابتا عندك على وجه الظن لا اليقين، فلم تجد بدّا في العبارة عن ثباته عندك على ذلك الوجه، من ذكر شطرى الجملة مدخلا عليهما فعل الحسبان، حتى يتم لك غرضك.
Question
If you ask: where, then, in the verse is the speech indicating the content that the reckoning requires?
فإن قلت: فأين الكلام الدال على المضمون الذي يقتضيه الحسبان في الآية؟
Answer
I say: it is in His words "that they will be left to say 'We believe' while they are not tried." The sense of it is: "Did they reckon that they would be left untried because of their saying 'We believe'?" So "being left" is the first object of "reckon," and "because of their saying 'We believe'" is the predicate. As for "untried," it completes the "leaving," because it belongs to the "leaving" that carries the sense of "making into," as in the line: "So I left him a carcass for the beasts of prey, tearing at him" [1]. Do you not see that, before bringing in the verb of reckoning, you could say: "Their being left untried is because of their saying 'We believe'," meaning "[this is] established and settled," before the lām?
قلت: هو في قوله أَنْ يُتْرَكُوا أَنْ يَقُولُوا آمَنَّا وَهُمْ لا يُفْتَنُونَ وذلك أن تقديره: أحسبوا تركهم غير مفتونين، لقولهم: آمنا، فالترك أول مفعولي حسب، ولقولهم: آمنا، هو الخبر. وأما «غير مفتونين» فتتمة الترك، لأنه من الترك الذي هو بمعنى التصيير، كقوله: فتركته جزر السّباع ينشنه «1» ألا ترى أنك قبل المجيء بالحسبان، تقدر أن تقول: تركهم غير مفتونين، لقولهم: آمنا، على تقدير: حاصل ومستقر، قبل اللام.
Question
If you ask: "that they say" is the reason for their being left untried, so how can it stand as the predicate of a subject?
فإن قلت: أَنْ يَقُولُوا هو علة تركهم غير مفتونين، فكيف يصح أن يقع خبر مبتدأ؟
Answer
I say: just as you say "his going out was for fear of evil" and "his beating was for discipline," while "discipline" and "fear" in your saying "I went out for fear of evil" and "I beat him for discipline" are two reasons. You also say "I reckoned his going out to be for fear of evil" and "I supposed his beating to be for discipline," making the two [phrases] objects, just as you made them subject
قلت: كما تقول خروجه لمخافة الشر، وضربه للتأديب، وقد كان التأديب والمخافة في قولك: خرجت مخافة الشر، وضربته تأديبا: تعليلين. وتقول أيضا: حسبت خروجه لمخافة الشر، وظننت ضربه للتأديب، فتجعلهما مفعولين كما جعلتهما مبتدأ
Vol. 3, p. 439
and predicate. Fitna (trial) is testing through the hardships of religious obligation: leaving one's homeland, striving against enemies, and all the arduous acts of obedience, abandoning desires and pleasures; and through poverty and drought, and the various kinds of calamities to persons and property; and through patiently enduring the unbelievers' harm, scheming, and injury. The meaning is: Did those who made the words of the testimony run on their tongues and outwardly professed faith think that they would be left thereby untested? No, God will test them with all kinds of trials, until He examines their patience, the firmness of their footing, the soundness of their beliefs and the purity of their intentions, so that the sincere is distinguished from the insincere, the firmly rooted in religion from the wavering, and the steadfast from the one who worships on an edge, as He said: "You will surely be tested in your wealth and in yourselves, and you will surely hear from those who were given the Book before you and from those who associated others with God much hurt; but if you are patient and fear God, that is among the matters requiring resolve." It is reported that it was revealed about some of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ who had become anxious over the harm done by the polytheists. It is also said: about 'Ammar ibn Yasir, who was being tortured for God's sake. And it is said: about some people who had become Muslims in Mecca, whereupon the Emigrants wrote to them: "Your Islam will not be accepted from you until you emigrate." So they set out, and the polytheists pursued them and brought them back; and when this was revealed, [the Emigrants] wrote it to them, and they set out again, and the polytheists pursued them and fought them; some of them were killed and some escaped. And it is said: about Mihja' ibn 'Abdullah, the freedman of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab ؓ who was the first Muslim killed on the Day of Badr; 'Amir ibn al-Hadrami shot him, and the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Mihja' is the master of the martyrs, and he is the first of this community to be called to the gate of Paradise" [1]; and his parents and his wife were distraught over him. "We certainly tried" is connected to "Do they think" or to "they are not tried," as in your saying: "Why should so-and-so not be tested, when one better than he was tested?" meaning that the followers of the prophets (peace be upon them) before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations like what has befallen these, or worse, and they were patient, as He said: "How many a prophet has fought, and with him many godly men, and they did not weaken..." (the verse). And from the Prophet ﷺ: "Among those before you was one who would be seized and a saw placed on his head and split into two halves, and that would not turn him from his religion; and he would be combed with iron combs [that stripped] the flesh and sinew from his bone, and that would not turn him from his religion" [2]. "God will surely know," by the test, "those who are truthful" in faith "and will surely know the liars" in it.
وخبرا. والفتنة: الامتحان بشدائد التكليف: من مفارقة الأوطان، ومجاهدة الأعداء، وسائر الطاعات الشاقة، وهجر الشهوات والملاذ، وبالفقر والقحط، وأنواع المصائب في الأنفس والأموال. وبمصابرة الكفار على أذاهم وكيدهم وضرارهم. والمعنى: أحسب الذين أجروا كلمة الشهادة على ألسنتهم وأظهروا القول بالإيمان: أنهم يتركون بذلك غير ممتحنين، بل يمحنهم الله بضروب المحن، حتى يبلو صبرهم، وثبات أقدامهم، وصحة عقائدهم، ونصوع نياتهم، ليتميز المخلص من غير المخلص، والراسخ في الدين من المضطرب، والمتمكن من العابد على حرف، كما قال لَتُبْلَوُنَّ فِي أَمْوالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَلَتَسْمَعُنَّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا أَذىً كَثِيراً وَإِنْ تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا فَإِنَّ ذلِكَ مِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ وروى أنها نزلت في ناس من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قد جزعوا من أذى المشركين. وقيل في عمار بن ياسر: وكان يعذب في الله. وقيل: في ناس أسلموا بمكة، فكتب إليهم المهاجرون: لا يقبل منكم إسلامكم حتى تهاجروا، فخرجوا فتبعهم المشركون فردّوهم، فلما نزلت كتبوا بها إليهم، فخرجوا فاتبعهم المشركون فقاتلوهم، فمنهم من قتل ومنهم من نجا. وقيل: في مهجع بن عبد الله مولى عمر بن الخطاب رضى الله عنه، وهو أوّل قتيل من المسلمين يوم بدر، رماه عامر بن الحضرمي فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: سيد الشهداء مهجع، وهو أول من يدعى إلى باب الجنة من هذه الأمة «1» ، فجزع عليه أبواه وامرأته وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا موصول بأحسب أو بلا يفتنون، كقولك: ألا يمتحن فلان وقد امتحن من هو خير منه، يعنى: أن أتباع الأنبياء عليهم السلام قبلهم، قد أصابهم من الفتن والمحن نحو ما أصابهم. أو ما هو أشدّ منه فصبروا، كما قال: وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ قاتَلَ مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ فَما وَهَنُوا … الآية وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «قد كان من قبلكم يؤخذ فيوضع المنشار على رأسه فيفرق فرقتين، ما يصرفه ذلك عن دينه، ويمشط بأمشاط الحديد ما دون عظمه من لحم وعصب، ما يصرفه ذلك عن دينه» «2» فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ بالامتحان الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا في الإيمان وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْكاذِبِينَ فيه.
Question
If you ask: How [so], when He has known that from eternity?
فإن قلت: كيف وهو عالم بذلك فيما لم يزل؟
Answer
I say: He has always known it as non-existent, but does not know it as existent except when it exists [3]. The meaning is:
قلت: لم يزل يعلمه معدوما، ولا يعلمه موجودا إلا إذا وجد «3» ، والمعنى:
Vol. 3, p. 440
that the truthful among them be distinguished from the liar. It may also be a promise and a threat, as if He had said: "He will surely reward those who were truthful and surely punish the liars." 'Ali ؓ and al-Zuhri read "wa-layu'limannā" (from i'lām, informing), meaning: "God will surely make the people know who they are," or "He will surely mark them with a sign by which they are recognized: the whiteness or blackness of faces, the kohl-lined look or the blueness of eyes."
وليتميزن الصادق منهم من الكاذب. ويجوز أن يكون وعدا ووعيدا، كأنه قال: وليثيبن الذين صدقوا وليعاقبنّ الكاذبين. وقرأ على رضى الله عنه والزهري: وليعلمنّ، من الإعلام، أى: وليعرفنهم الله الناس من هم. أو ليسمنهم بعلامة يعرفون بها من بياض الوجوه وسوادها، وكحل العيون وزرقتها.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 3, p. 438

1. (1) . تقدم شرح هذا الشاهد بالجزء الأول صفحة 75 فراجعه إن شئت اه مصححه.
Vol. 3, p. 439
1. (1). Al-Tha'labi mentioned it from Muqatil, who said: "These two verses were revealed about Mihja' ibn 'Abdullah, the freedman of 'Umar, who was the first Muslim killed on the Day of Badr; 'Amir ibn al-Hadrami shot him with an arrow and killed him. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Mihja' is the master of the martyrs, and he is the first of this community to be called to the gate of Paradise.'" His chain to Muqatil is at the beginning of his book. In the Dala'il of Ibn Abi Shayba, via al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, he said: "The first to be martyred on the day of Badr was Mihja', the freedman of 'Umar."
2. Al-Bukhari transcribed it from the hadith of Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, and it is fuller there.
3. Mahmud [al-Zamakhshari] said: "If you say, 'He has always known the truthful and the liars before the test, so what is the point of this statement?' I say: He has always known it as non-existent, but does not know it as existent except when it exists." Ahmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: In what he mentioned there is an implication of a corrupt doctrine, namely the belief that knowledge of what is [now] occurring differs from knowledge that it will occur. The truth is that God's knowledge is one, and it relates to the existent at the time of its existence, before it, and after it, as it is; and the point of mentioning knowledge here, though it precedes the existence of the thing known, is to alert, by mentioning the cause, to the effect, namely recompense, as if He had said: "We shall know them, so We shall recompense them according to Our knowledge of them." And God knows best.

3. . قال محمود: «إن قلت هو لم يزل يعلم الصادقين والكاذبين قبل الامتحان، فما وجه هذا الكلام؟ قلت: لم يزل يعلمه معدوما ولا يعلمه موجودا إلا إذا وجد» قال أحمد: فيما ذكر إيهام بمذهب فاسد، وهو اعتقاد أن العلم بالكائن غير العلم بأن سيكون، والحق أن علم الله تعالى واحد يتعلق بالموجود زمان وجوده وقبله وبعده على ما هو عليه، وفائدة ذكر العلم هاهنا وإن كان سابقا على وجود المعلوم: التنبيه بالسبب على المسبب وهو الجزاء، كأنه قال تعالى: لنعلمنهم فلنجازينهم بحسب علمه فيهم، والله أعلم.
03
Q 29:4 · Vol. 3, p. 440

Verse 4

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Or do those who do evil deeds think that they can outstrip Us? Evil is what they judge (4)
أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ أَنْ يَسْبِقُونا ساءَ ما يَحْكُمُونَ (4)
Vol. 3, p. 440
"That they can outstrip Us" means: that they can escape Us, i.e. recompense will inevitably overtake them, though they did not hope to escape and never spoke to themselves of it; but because of their heedlessness, their scant reflection on the outcome and their persistence in sins, they are in the position of one who supposes that and hopes for it. Its like is: "You can never frustrate [God] in the earth," and "Let not those who disbelieve think they have outstripped; they cannot frustrate [Us]."
أَنْ يَسْبِقُونا أن يفوتونا، يعنى أنّ الجزاء يلحقهم لا محالة، وهم لم يطمعوا في الفوت، ولم يحدّثوا به نفوسهم، ولكنهم لغفلتهم وقلة فكرهم في العاقبة وإصرارهم على المعاصي: في صورة من يقدر ذلك ويطمع فيه. ونظيره وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ، وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَبَقُوا إِنَّهُمْ لا يُعْجِزُونَ.
Question
If you ask: Where are the two objects of "ḥasiba"?
فإن قلت: أين مفعولا «حسب» ؟
Answer
I say: the clause of "that" contains a predicate and a subject, which takes the place of the two objects, as in His words: "Or did you think that you would enter Paradise?" It is also possible that "ḥasiba" is taken in the sense of "estimate," and "am" is detached [i.e. "rather"]. The sense of the turning-away in it is that this reckoning is more false than the first reckoning, because that one supposes he will not be tested for his faith, while this one thinks he will not be recompensed for his evil deeds. "Evil is what they judge": how evil is that which they judge, this judgment of theirs; or: what an evil judgment they pass, this judgment of theirs, with the object of condemnation omitted.
قلت: اشتمال صلة أن على مسند ومسند إليه سدّ مسدّ المفعولين، كقوله تعالى أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ ويجوز أن يضمن حسب معنى قدر وأم منقطعة. ومعنى الإضراب فيها: أن هذا الحسبان أبطل من الحسبان الأوّل، لأن ذاك يقدر أنه لا يمتحن لإيمانه، وهذا يظن أنه لا يجازى بمساويه ساءَ ما يَحْكُمُونَ بئس الذي يحكمونه حكمهم هذا. أو بئس حكما يحكمونه حكمهم هذا، فحذف المخصوص بالذم.
04
Q 29:5 · Vol. 3, pp. 440–441

Verse 5

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Whoever hopes for the meeting with God, then the term appointed by God is surely coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (5)
مَنْ كانَ يَرْجُوا لِقاءَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ لَآتٍ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ (5)
Vol. 3, p. 440
"The meeting with God" is a figure for arriving at the outcome: meeting the angel of death, the resurrection, the reckoning and the recompense. That state is likened to the state of a servant who comes before his master after a long absence, the master having been informed of what he did and what he left undone; so either he meets him with joy and welcome because he approved of his deeds, or with the opposite because he was displeased by them. So the meaning of "whoever hopes for the meeting with God" is: whoever longs for that state and to meet in it honor and glad tidings from God. "Then the term of God," which is death, "is surely coming," without fail; so let him hasten to the righteous deed that will confirm his hope, make good his longing, and earn him nearness and favor with God. "And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing," from whom nothing escapes of what His servants say and do; so He is worthy of being feared and held in awe. It is also said that "yarjū" means "fears," from the saying of the Hudhali describing a honey-gatherer:
لقاء الله: مثل للوصول إلى العاقبة، من تلقى ملك الموت، والبعث، والحساب، والجزاء: مثلت تلك الحال بحال عبد قدم على سيده بعد عهد طويل، وقد اطلع مولاه على ما كان يأتى ويذر، فإما أن يلقاه ببشر وترحيب لما رضى من أفعاله، أو بضد ذلك لما سخطه منها، فمعنى قوله مَنْ كانَ يَرْجُوا لِقاءَ اللَّهِ: من كان يأمل تلك الحال. وأن يلقى فيها الكرامة من الله والبشر فَإِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ وهو الموت لَآتٍ لا محالة، فليبادر العمل الصالح الذي يصدق رجاءه، ويحقق أمله، ويكتسب به القربة عند الله والزلفى وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ الذي لا يخفى عليه شيء مما يقوله عباده ومما يفعلونه، فهو حقيق بالتقوى والخشية. وقيل يَرْجُوا: يخاف من قول الهذلي في صفة عسال:
Vol. 3, p. 441
"When the drones stung him he did not fear their sting" [1].
إذا لسعته الدّبر لم يرج لسعها «1»
Question
If you ask: "The term of God is surely coming" — how can this be the answer to the conditional?
فإن قلت: فإن أجل الله لآت، كيف وقع جوابا للشرط؟
Answer
I say: when it is known that what is meant by "meeting God" is that figurative state, and that the time in which that state occurs is the term fixed for death, it is as if He had said: "Whoever hopes for the meeting with God, then the meeting with God is surely coming," because the term is where the meeting takes place; just as you say: "Whoever hopes to meet the king, Friday is near," when it is known that he sits for the people on Friday.
قلت: إذا علم أن لقاء الله عنيت به تلك الحال الممثلة والوقت الذي تقع فيه تلك الحال هو الأجل المضروب للموت: فكأنه قال: من كان يرجو لقاء الله فإن لقاء الله لآت، لأن الأجل واقع فيه اللقاء، كما تقول: من كان يرجو لقاء الملك فإن يوم الجمعة قريب، إذا علم أنه يقعد للناس يوم الجمعة.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 441
1. (1). "When the drones stung him he did not fear their sting... and he stayed close to them in the home of the Nub bees, rich in honey" — by Abu Dhu'ayb, describing a honey-gatherer. "Al-dabr" (with fatḥa or kasra on the dāl) means the male bees and wasps. It is also transmitted thus: "lam yarji," i.e. "he did not fear their sting when they wished to sting him," or "when they stung him in fact he did not fear the like of it," or "he did not watch for it or care about it." "Ḥālafahā" means he stayed close to them. It is transmitted with a dotted khā' [khālafahā], i.e. he opposed their wish, or came behind them after they went out grazing. "Al-nūb" is a kind of bee, singular "nā'ib," because it goes to its hive turn after turn; "'awāsil" means abounding in honey. It is also transmitted "'awāmil" with a mīm, because they make honey.
2. Mahmud said: "Those meant are one of two groups: either Muslims whose misdeeds are minor sins submerged by good deeds, or people who believed and did righteous deeds after disbelief, for Islam cancels what came before it." Ahmad said: He has fenced off a vast area of God's mercy, on the basis of his corrupt principle that threats [of punishment] are binding on one who commits major sins unless he repents; and he makes the expiation of minor sins absolute even without repentance when good deeds submerge them. Both principles are Qadari and to be avoided. And God grants success.
1. (1) . إذا لسعته الدبر لم يرج لسعها
…. وحالفها في بيت نوب عواسل لأبى ذؤيب، يصف عسالا يجتنى العسل: بأنه إذا لسعته الدبر- بالفتح والكسر-: ذكور النحل والزنابير. وروى كذلك: لم يرج، أى: لم يخف لسعها إذا أرادت لسعه. أو لسعته بالفعل لم يخف من مثله، أو لم يرتقبه ويعتنى به، وحالفها: أى لازمها. ويروى بالمعجمة، أى: خالف مرادها. أو جاء خلفها بعد أن خرجت ترعى. والنوب: ضرب من النحل واحده نائب، لأنه يذهب إلى بيته نوبة بعد نوبة، عواسل: كثيرة العسل. وروى: عوامل، بالميم لأنها تعمل العسل.
2. . قال محمود: «المراد بهؤلاء أحد فريقين: إما قوم مسلمون سيئاتهم صغائر مغمورة بالحسنات، وإما قوم آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات بعد كفر فالإسلام يجب ما قبله» قال أحمد: حجر واسعا من رحمة الله تعالى، بناء على أصله الفاسد في وجوب الوعيد على مرتكب السيئات الكبائر لا بالتوبة، وأطلق تكفير الصغائر وإن لم تكن توبة إذا غمرتها الحسنات، وكلا الأصلين قدرى مجتنب، والله الموفق.

Q 29:6 · Vol. 3, p. 441

Verse 6

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And whoever strives only strives for himself. Indeed God is free of need of all the worlds (6)
وَمَنْ جاهَدَ فَإِنَّما يُجاهِدُ لِنَفْسِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعالَمِينَ (6)
Vol. 3, p. 441
"Whoever strives" against his own soul, in restraining it from what it commands and constraining it to what it resists, "strives only for it," because the benefit of that returns to it. God, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded and forbade only out of mercy for His servants, while He is independent of them and of their obedience.
وَمَنْ جاهَدَ نفسه في منعها ما تأمر به وحملها على ما تأباه فَإِنَّما يُجاهِدُ لها، لأن منفعة ذلك راجعة إليها، وإنما أمر الله عز وجل ونهى، رحمة لعباده وهو الغنى عنهم وعن طاعتهم.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 441

Q 29:7 · Vol. 3, p. 441

Verse 7

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We shall surely remove from them their misdeeds, and We shall surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do (7)
وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَنُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَحْسَنَ الَّذِي كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (7)
Vol. 3, p. 441
Either He means Muslim, righteous people who have erred in some of their actions, their misdeeds being submerged by their good deeds, so He expiates them for them, i.e. cancels their punishment through the reward of the good deeds, "and rewards them according to the best of what they used to do," i.e. the best recompense for their deeds; or He means polytheists who believed and did righteous deeds, so God, the Mighty and Majestic, expiates their misdeeds by cancelling the punishment of their previous disbelief and sins, and rewards them with the best recompense for their deeds in Islam [2].
إما أن يريد قوما مسلمين صالحين قد أساءوا في بعض أعمالهم وسيئاتهم مغمورة بحسناتهم فهو يكفرها عنهم، أى يسقط عقابها بثواب الحسنات ويجزيهم أحسن الذي كانوا يعملون، أى: أحسن جزاء أعمالهم: وإما قوما مشركين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات، فالله عز وجل يكفر سيئاتهم بأن يسقط عقاب ما تقدم لهم من الكفر والمعاصي ويجزيهم أحسن جزاء أعمالهم في الإسلام «2» .
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 441

Q 29:8 · Vol. 3, pp. 441–443

Verse 8

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents; but if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do (8)
وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ حُسْناً وَإِنْ جاهَداكَ لِتُشْرِكَ بِي ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ فَلا تُطِعْهُما إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ (8)
Vol. 3, p. 442
"Waṣṣā" [to enjoin] has the same ruling as "amara" [to command] in meaning and usage. One says "waṣṣaytu Zaydan bi-an yaf'ala khayran" as one says "amartuhu bi-an yaf'ala." Among its examples is the verse of the author of the Iṣlāḥ: "A woman of Dhubyan enjoined her sons that the velvet cloaks and the leather sacks are yours to seize" [1] — as if he had said: she commanded them to plunder them. And among it is His saying: "And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons" i.e. he enjoined them with the word of divine oneness and commanded them to it. And your saying "waṣṣaytu Zaydan bi-'Amr" means: I enjoined him to take care of 'Amr and look after him, and the like. Likewise the meaning of His words "And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents" is: We enjoined him to give his parents goodness, or to render his parents goodness, i.e. an act that is good, or something good in itself to the utmost degree, like His words "and speak to people good [words]." It is also read "ḥusnan" and "iḥsānan." It is also possible to treat "ḥusnan" as in your saying "Zaydan!" with an implied "strike" when you see him ready to be struck, so it is put in the accusative by an implied "do for them [both] good" or "do to them [both] good," because the enjoining of [kindness to] them indicates it, and what follows corresponds to it, as if He had said: "We said: Do good to them both" and "do not obey them" in polytheism if they urge you to it. On this interpretation, if one pauses at "to his parents" and begins "ḥusnan," the pause is good; on the first interpretation an implied "saying" is required, meaning: "and We said: if they strive with you, O man, [to make you associate with Me] that of which you have no knowledge," i.e. you have no knowledge of its divinity. The meaning of negating knowledge is negating the thing known, as if He had said: to make you associate with Me something that cannot be a god and cannot be sound. He enjoined him concerning his parents and commanded him to be kind to them, then alerted him, by forbidding obedience to them when they want him to do what was mentioned, that every right, however great, falls away when God's right comes, and that there is no obedience to a creature in disobedience to the Creator. Then He said: "To Me is the return of whoever of you believed and whoever associated, and I shall recompense you your due recompense." In this are two things. One: that recompense is Mine, so do not think of being harsh to your parents and undutiful to them because of their polytheism, nor withhold from them your kindness and goodness in this world, just as I do not withhold My provision from them. The second: the warning against following them in polytheism, and the urging to steadfastness and uprightness in religion by mentioning the return and the threat. It is reported that when Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas al-Zuhri ؓ became a Muslim, his mother, Hamna daughter of Abu Sufyan ibn Umayya ibn 'Abd Shams, said: "O Sa'd, I have heard that you have apostatized. By God, no roof of a house will shade me from the sun
«وصى» حكمه حكم «أمر» في معناه وتصرفه. يقال: وصيت زيدا بأن يفعل خيرا، كما تقول: أمرته بأن يفعل. ومنه بيت الإصلاح: وذبيانيّة وصّت بنيها … بأن كذب القراطف والقروف «1» كما لو قال: أمرتهم بأن ينتهبوها. ومنه قوله تعالى وَوَصَّى بِها إِبْراهِيمُ بَنِيهِ أى وصاهم بكلمة التوحيد وأمرهم بها، وقولك: وصيت زيدا بعمرو، معناه: وصيته بتعهد عمرو ومراعاته ونحو ذلك، وكذلك معنى قوله وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ حُسْناً: وصيناه بإيتاء والديه حسنا، أو بإيلاء والديه حسنا، أى: فعلا ذا حسن، أو ما هو في ذاته حسن لفرط حسنه، كقوله تعالى وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً وقرئ: حسنا. وإحسانا. ويجوز أن تجعل حُسْناً من باب قولك: زيدا، بإضمار «أضرب» إذا رأيته متهيئا للضرب، فتنصبه بإضمار أو لهما. أو افعل بهما، لأن التوصية بهما دالة عليه، وما بعده مطابق له، كأنه قال: قلنا أو لهما معروفا وفَلا تُطِعْهُما في الشرك إذا حملاك عليه. وعلى هذا التفسير إن وقف على بِوالِدَيْهِ وابتدأ حُسْناً حسن الوقف، وعلى التفسير الأول لا بد من إضمار القول، معناه: وقلنا إن جاهداك أيها الإنسان ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ أى لا علم لك بإلهيته. والمراد بنفي العلم: نفى المعلوم، كأنه قال: لتشرك بى شيئا لا يصح أن يكون إلها ولا يستقيم: وصاه بوالديه وأمره بالإحسان إليهما، ثم نبه بنهيه عن طاعتهما إذا أراداه على ما ذكر، على أن كل حق وإن عظم ساقط إذا جاء حق الله، وأنه لا طاعة لمخلوق في معصية الخالق، ثم قال: إلىّ مرجع من آمن منكم ومن أشرك، فأجازيكم حق جزائكم. وفيه شيئان، أحدهما: أن الجزاء إلىّ، فلا تحدث نفسك بجفوة والديك وعقوقهما لشركهما، ولا تحرمهما برك ومعروفك في الدنيا، كما أنى لا أمنعهما رزقي. والثاني: التحذير من متابعتهما على الشرك، والحث على الثبات والاستقامة في الدين بذكر المرجع والوعيد. روى أن سعد بن أبى وقاص الزهري رضى الله عنه حين أسلم قالت أمّه- وهي حمنة بنت أبى سفيان بن أمية بن عبد شمس-: يا سعد، بلغني أنك قد صبأت، فو الله لا يظلني سقف بيت من الضح «2»
Vol. 3, p. 443
and the wind, and food and drink are forbidden to me until you disbelieve in Muhammad" — and he was her most beloved child. Sa'd refused, and she remained so for three days. Sa'd came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and complained to him, so this verse was revealed, and the one in Luqman, and the one in al-Ahqaf; and the Messenger of God ﷺ commanded him to treat her gently and win her over with kindness [1]. It is also reported that it was revealed about 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a al-Makhzumi. That was because he emigrated with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab ؓ as travel companions until they reached Medina [2]. Then Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and al-Harith ibn Hisham — his maternal half-brothers, whose mother was Asma' daughter of Makhrama, a woman of Banu Tamim of Banu Hanzala — came to 'Ayyash and said to him: "Part of Muhammad's religion is joining kinship ties and dutifulness to parents, and you have left your mother neither eating nor drinking nor taking shelter in a house until she sees you, and she loves you more than we do; so come out with us." And they worked on him at the hump and the withers [3]. He consulted 'Umar ؓ who said: "They are deceiving you, and I promise you that I will divide my wealth between you and me." But they kept at him until he obeyed them and disobeyed 'Umar. 'Umar said to him: "Since you have disobeyed me, take my she-camel, for there is no camel in the world that can catch her; and if anything about them makes you suspicious, turn back." When they reached al-Bayda', Abu Jahl said: "My camel has tired; carry me with you." He said, "Yes," and dismounted to make [the saddle] comfortable for himself and him; but they seized him and bound him fast, and each of them whipped him a hundred lashes, and they took him to his mother, who said: "You will remain in torment until you abandon Muhammad's religion." So this was revealed.
والريج، وإن الطعام والشراب علىّ حرام حتى تكفر بمحمد- وكان أحبّ ولدها إليها- فأبى سعد وبقيت ثلاثة أيام كذلك، فجاء سعد إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وشكا إليه، فنزلت هذه الآية والتي في لقمان والتي في الأحقاف، فأمره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يداريها ويترضاها بالإحسان «1» . وروى أنها نزلت في عياش بن أبى ربيعة المخزومي، وذلك أنه هاجر مع عمر بن الخطاب رضى الله عنهما مترافقين حتى نزلا المدينة «2» ، فخرج أبو جهل بن هشام والحرث بن هشام- أخواه لأمه أسماء بنت مخرمة: امرأة من بنى تميم من بنى حنظلة- فنزلا بعياش وقالا له: إن من دين محمد صلة الأرحام وبر الوالدين، وقد تركت أمّك لا تطعم ولا تشرب ولا تأوى بيتا حتى تراك، وهي أشدّ حبا لك منا فاخرج معنا، وفتلا منه في الذروة والغارب «3» فاستشار عمر رضى الله عنه فقال: هما يخدعانك، ولك علىّ أن أقسم مالى بيني وبينك، فما زالا به حتى أطاعهما وعصى عمر، فقال له عمر: أما إذ عصيتني فخذ ناقتي، فليس في الدنيا بعير يلحقها، فإن رابك منهما ريب فارجع، فلما انتهوا إلى البيداء قال أبو جهل: إن ناقتي قد كلت فاحملني معك. قال: نعم، فنزل ليوطئ لنفسه وله، فأخذاه وشدّاه وثاقا، وجلده كل واحد منهما مائة جلدة، وذهبا به إلى أمه فقالت: لا تزال في عذاب حتى ترجع عن دين محمد، فنزلت.
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 3, p. 441
1. (1). "When the drones stung him he did not fear their sting... and he stayed close to them in the home of the Nub bees, rich in honey" — by Abu Dhu'ayb, describing a honey-gatherer. "Al-dabr" (with fatḥa or kasra on the dāl) means the male bees and wasps. It is also transmitted thus: "lam yarji," i.e. "he did not fear their sting when they wished to sting him," or "when they stung him in fact he did not fear the like of it," or "he did not watch for it or care about it." "Ḥālafahā" means he stayed close to them. It is transmitted with a dotted khā' [khālafahā], i.e. he opposed their wish, or came behind them after they went out grazing. "Al-nūb" is a kind of bee, singular "nā'ib," because it goes to its hive turn after turn; "'awāsil" means abounding in honey. It is also transmitted "'awāmil" with a mīm, because they make honey.
2. Mahmud said: "Those meant are one of two groups: either Muslims whose misdeeds are minor sins submerged by good deeds, or people who believed and did righteous deeds after disbelief, for Islam cancels what came before it." Ahmad said: He has fenced off a vast area of God's mercy, on the basis of his corrupt principle that threats [of punishment] are binding on one who commits major sins unless he repents; and he makes the expiation of minor sins absolute even without repentance when good deeds submerge them. Both principles are Qadari and to be avoided. And God grants success.
1. (1) . إذا لسعته الدبر لم يرج لسعها
…. وحالفها في بيت نوب عواسل لأبى ذؤيب، يصف عسالا يجتنى العسل: بأنه إذا لسعته الدبر- بالفتح والكسر-: ذكور النحل والزنابير. وروى كذلك: لم يرج، أى: لم يخف لسعها إذا أرادت لسعه. أو لسعته بالفعل لم يخف من مثله، أو لم يرتقبه ويعتنى به، وحالفها: أى لازمها. ويروى بالمعجمة، أى: خالف مرادها. أو جاء خلفها بعد أن خرجت ترعى. والنوب: ضرب من النحل واحده نائب، لأنه يذهب إلى بيته نوبة بعد نوبة، عواسل: كثيرة العسل. وروى: عوامل، بالميم لأنها تعمل العسل.
2. . قال محمود: «المراد بهؤلاء أحد فريقين: إما قوم مسلمون سيئاتهم صغائر مغمورة بالحسنات، وإما قوم آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات بعد كفر فالإسلام يجب ما قبله» قال أحمد: حجر واسعا من رحمة الله تعالى، بناء على أصله الفاسد في وجوب الوعيد على مرتكب السيئات الكبائر لا بالتوبة، وأطلق تكفير الصغائر وإن لم تكن توبة إذا غمرتها الحسنات، وكلا الأصلين قدرى مجتنب، والله الموفق.
Vol. 3, p. 442

1. (1) . لمعقر بن حمار البارقي، أنشده ابن السكيت في كتابه المسمى: إصلاح المنطق، أى: امرأة منسوبة إلى قبيلة ذبيان وصت بنيها. وأن مخففة من الثقيلة، واسمها ضمير الشأن، وخبرها: كذب، وهو قد يكون بمعنى وجب كما في الصحاح. وفي الحديث: ثلاثة أسفار كذبن عليكم، أى: وجبن. وعن عمر رضى الله عنه: كذب عليكم الحج، أى وجب. وفي الكلام معنى الحث والإغراء. والقراطف: جمع قرطف، وهو القطيفة المخملة. والقروف: أوعية من أدم يجعل فيها اللحم المشوى. والقرف- بالكسر-: المقشر. والقرفة: قشر يداوى به. والقرف- بالفتح- وعاء من جلد يدبغ بالقرفة. واقترف، واقترب: متقاربان لفظا ومعنى، أى: وصتهم باغتنامها وحفظها معهم. [.....]
2. . قوله «من الضح» في الصحاح «الضح» : الشمس. وفي الحديث: «لا يقعدن أحدكم بين الضح والظل، فانه مقعد الشيطان» اه. (ع)
Vol. 3, p. 443

3. . قوله «وفتلا منه في الذروة والغارب» في الصحاح: ما زال فلان يفتل من فلان في الذروة والغارب، أى: يدور من وراء خديعته. (ع)
08
Q 29:9 · Vol. 3, p. 443

Verse 9

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We shall surely admit them among the righteous (9)
وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَنُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ فِي الصَّالِحِينَ (9)
Vol. 3, p. 443
"Among the righteous" means into their number. Righteousness is among the loftiest attributes of the believers, and it is what the prophets of God wished for. God the Exalted said, relating from Solomon ﷺ: "and admit me, by Your mercy, among Your righteous servants," and of Abraham ﷺ: "and indeed in the Hereafter he is among the righteous." Or [it means] into the abode of the righteous, which is Paradise, and this is like His words: "Whoever obeys God and the Messenger, those are with the ones whom God has favored" (the verse).
فِي الصَّالِحِينَ في جملتهم. والصلاح من أبلغ صفات المؤمنين، وهو متمنى أنبياء الله. قال الله تعالى حكاية عن سليمان عليه السلام وَأَدْخِلْنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِي عِبادِكَ الصَّالِحِينَ وقال في إبراهيم عليه السلام: وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ أو في مدخل الصالحين وهي الجنة، وهذا نحو قوله تعالى وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ فَأُولئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ الآية.

Q 29:10–11 · Vol. 3, pp. 443–444

Verses 10 to 11

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And among the people are those who say, "We believe in God," but when they are harmed in God's cause, they make people's persecution like God's punishment; and if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "We were with you." Is not God most knowing of what is in the breasts of all the worlds? (10) And God will surely know those who believe, and He will surely know the hypocrites (11)
وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ فَإِذا أُوذِيَ فِي اللَّهِ جَعَلَ فِتْنَةَ النَّاسِ كَعَذابِ اللَّهِ وَلَئِنْ جاءَ نَصْرٌ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّا كُنَّا مَعَكُمْ أَوَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَعْلَمَ بِما فِي صُدُورِ الْعالَمِينَ (10) وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ (11)
Vol. 3, p. 444
These are people who believed with their tongues, but when harm from the unbelievers touched them — which is what is meant by "people's persecution" — it turned them away from faith, just as God's punishment turns the believers away from unbelief; or as it ought to be that God's punishment should turn [them away]. And when God gives victory to the believers and grants them spoils, they confront them and say "We were with you," i.e. followers of your religion alongside you, firm in it as you were firm, and no one was able to put us to the test; so give us our share of the spoils. Then He, glory be to Him, informed that He knows best "what is in the breasts of the worlds" of the peoples, and from that is what the breasts of these conceal of hypocrisy; and this is a disclosure from Him to the believers of what they were hiding. Then He made a promise to the believers and a threat to the hypocrites. It is also read "layaqūlunna" with a fatḥa on the lām.
هم ناس كانوا يؤمنون بألسنتهم، فإذا مسهم أذى من الكفار وهو المراد بفتنة الناس، كان ذلك صارفا لهم عن الإيمان، كما أن عذاب الله صارف للمؤمنين عن الكفر. أو كما يجب أن يكون عذاب الله صارفا. وإذا نصر الله المؤمنين وغنمهم اعترضوهم وقالوا إِنَّا كُنَّا مَعَكُمْ أى مشايعين لكم في دينكم، ثابتين عليه ثباتكم، ما قدر أحد أن يفتننا، فأعطونا نصيبنا من المغنم. ثم أخبر سبحانه أنه أعلم بِما فِي صُدُورِ الْعالَمِينَ من العالمين بما في صدورهم، ومن ذلك ما تكنّ صدور هؤلاء من النفاق، وهذا إطلاع منه للمؤمنين على ما أبطنوه، ثم وعد المؤمنين وأوعد المنافقين. وقرئ: ليقولنّ، بفتح اللام.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 3, p. 443
Translation in progress.
1. (1) . ذكره الواحدي والثعلبي والواقدي هكذا بغير سند والقصة في صحيح مسلم من حديث سعد بن أبى وقاص بغير هذا السياق.
2. . تقدم الكلام عليه في سورة النساء وهذا السياق أورده الثعلبي عن مقاتل وسنده إليه في أول كتابه، وأخرجه ابن إسحاق في المغازي ومن طريقه البزار قال: حدثني نافع عن ابن عمر عن عمر مطولا.
3. . قوله «وفتلا منه في الذروة والغارب» في الصحاح: ما زال فلان يفتل من فلان في الذروة والغارب، أى: يدور من وراء خديعته. (ع)
Vol. 3, p. 444
1. (1). Mahmud said: "Some of those who call themselves Muslims, when he wants to encourage his companion to a sin, says to him: 'Do this and its sin is on my neck.' Among it is what is told that a man submitted his needs to al-Mansur, and when he had fulfilled them, he said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have one more need, the greatest.' He said: 'And what is it?' He said: 'Your intercession in the place of gathering.' 'Amr said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, beware of these people, for they are highwaymen in a place of safety.'" Ahmad said: 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd was the first of the Qadaris who denied intercession, so beware of him. The verse does not correspond to the anecdote, but al-Zamakhshari proceeds on the basis that there is no difference between believing in intercession and believing that the unbelievers carry the sins of their followers, so he put the two on a single footing. We seek refuge in God from that. In His words "indeed they are liars" is a fine point from which one may argue for the soundness of a command being used in the sense of a report: for some people denied it and committed themselves to reinterpreting everything transmitted on that matter according to the original sense of command, but this was not complete for them in this verse, because God followed their words "and we will carry your sins," in imperative form, with His words "indeed they are liars," and the charge of lying applies only to reports.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «وبعض المتسمين بالإسلام إذا أراد أن يشجع صاحبه على ذنب قال له: افعل هذا وإثمه في عنقي. ومنه ما يحكى أن رجلا رفع إلى المنصور حوائجه فلما قضاها، قال يا أمير المؤمنين، بقيت لي إليك حاجة هي العظمى. قال: وما هي؟ قال: شفاعتك في المحشر. فقال عمرو: يا أمير المؤمنين، إياك وهؤلاء فهم قطاع الطريق في المأمن» قال أحمد: عمرو بن عبيد أول القدرية المنكرين للشفاعة فاحذره، وليست الآية مطابقة للحكاية، ولكن الزمخشري يبنى على أنه لا فرق بين اعتقاد الشفاعة واعتقاد أن الكفار يحملون خطايا أتباعهم، فلذلك ساقهما مساقا واحدا نعوذ بالله من ذلك. وفي قوله تعالى: إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ نكتة حسنة يستدل بها على صحة مجيء الأمر بمعنى الخبر، فان من الناس من أنكره والتزم تخريج جميع ما ورد في ذلك على أصل الأمر، ولم يتم له ذلك في هذه الآية، لأن الله تعالى أردف قولهم: ولنحمل خطاياكم، على صيغة الأمر بقوله إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ والتكذيب إنما يتطرق إلى الاخبار.
10
Q 29:12–13 · Vol. 3, pp. 444–445

Verses 12 to 13

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And those who disbelieve said to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will carry your sins." But they will not carry anything of their sins; indeed they are liars (12) And they will surely carry their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate (13)
وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبِعُوا سَبِيلَنا وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطاياكُمْ وَما هُمْ بِحامِلِينَ مِنْ خَطاياهُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ (12) وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ وَأَثْقالاً مَعَ أَثْقالِهِمْ وَلَيُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ عَمَّا كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ (13)
Vol. 3, p. 444
They commanded them to follow their way, which is the path they were on in their religion, and they commanded themselves to carry their sins, so they coordinated a command with a command; they meant: "Let these two come together in effect: that you follow our way and that we carry your sins." The meaning is: making the carrying contingent upon the following. This was the speech of the chiefs of Quraysh: they used to say to whoever of them believed, "We shall not be resurrected, neither we nor you; and if perchance it should be so, then we shall bear the sin on your behalf." And we see among those who call themselves Muslims one who follows their practice, saying to his companion, when he wants to encourage him to commit some grave offense: "Do this and its sin is on my neck." How many a weak commoner and ignoramus is deluded by such a guarantee! — and among that is what is told of Abu Ja'far al-Mansur, to whom one of the literalists (ahl al-ḥashw) submitted his needs, and when he had fulfilled them he said, "O Commander of the Faithful, the greatest need remains." He said, "And what is it?" He said, "Your intercession on the Day of Resurrection." 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd ؒ said to him: "Beware of these people, for they are highwaymen in a place of safety" [1]. If you ask: How could He call them
أمروهم باتباع سبيلهم وهي طريقتهم التي كانوا عليها في دينهم، وأمروا أنفسهم بحمل خطاياهم فعطف الأمر على الأمر، وأرادوا: ليجتمع هذان الأمران في الحصول أن تتبعوا سبيلنا وأن تحمل خطاياكم. والمعنى: تعليق الحمل بالاتباع، وهذا قول صناديد قريش: كانوا يقولون لمن آمن منهم: لا نبعث نحن ولا أنتم، فإن عسى كان ذلك فإنا نتحمل عنكم الإثم. ونرى في المتسمين بالإسلام من يستن بأولئك فيقول لصاحبه- إذا أراد أن يشجعه على ارتكاب بعض العظائم-: افعل هذا وإثمه في عنقي. وكم من مغرور بمثل هذا الضمان من ضعفة العامّة وجهلتهم- ومنه ما يحكى أنّ أبا جعفر المنصور رفع إليه بعض أهل الحشو حوائجه، فلما قضاها قال: يا أمير المؤمنين، بقيت الحاجة العظمى. قال: وما هي؟ قال شفاعتك يوم القيامة، فقال له عمرو بن عبيد رحمه الله: إياك وهؤلاء، فإنهم قطاع الطريق في المأمن «1» . فإن قلت: كيف سماهم
Vol. 3, p. 445
liars, when they only guaranteed something that God knew they were unable to fulfill? And one who guarantees what it is not known he can fulfill is not called a liar, neither when he guarantees nor when he fails, since in both cases he does not fall under the definition of the liar, who is one who reports a thing not as it is? I say: God likened their situation — since He knew that what they guaranteed they had no way to fulfill, so their guarantee in His sight was not in accord with the thing guaranteed — to the liars whose report is not in accord with what is reported. It is also possible that He means they are liars because they said that while their hearts were contrary to it, like the liars who promise something with the intention of breaking it in their hearts. "And they will surely carry their own burdens" meaning the burdens of themselves, "and burdens" meaning other burdens besides the sins they guaranteed to the believers to carry, and these are the burdens of those whom they caused to go astray; "and they will surely be questioned," a questioning of rebuke, "about what they used to fabricate," i.e. invent of lies and falsehoods. It is also read "min khaṭī'ātihim."
كاذبين، وإنما ضمنوا شيئا علم الله أنهم لا يقدرون على الوفاء به، وضامن ما لا يعلم اقتداره على الوفاء به، لا يسمى كاذبا لا حين ضمن ولا حين عجز، لأنه في الحالين لا يدخل تحت حدّ الكاذب وهو المخبر عن الشيء لا على ما هو عليه؟ قلت: شبه الله حالهم حيث علم أن ما ضمنوه لا طريق لهم إلى أن يفوا به، فكان ضمانهم عنده لا على ما عليه المضمون بالكاذبين الذين خبرهم لا على ما عليه لمخبر، عنه. ويجوز أن يريد أنهم كاذبون، لأنهم قالوا ذلك وقلوبهم على خلافه، كالكاذبين الذين يعدون الشيء وفي قلوبهم نية الخلف وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ أى أثقال أنفسهم وَأَثْقالًا يعنى أثّقالا أخر غير الخطايا التي ضمنوا للمؤمنين حملها، وهي أثقال الذين كانوا سببا في ضلالهم وَلَيُسْئَلُنَّ سؤال تقريع عَمَّا كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ أى يختلقون من الأكاذيب والأباطيل. وقرئ: من خطيآتهم.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 3, p. 444
1. (1). Mahmud said: "Some of those who call themselves Muslims, when he wants to encourage his companion to a sin, says to him: 'Do this and its sin is on my neck.' Among it is what is told that a man submitted his needs to al-Mansur, and when he had fulfilled them, he said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have one more need, the greatest.' He said: 'And what is it?' He said: 'Your intercession in the place of gathering.' 'Amr said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, beware of these people, for they are highwaymen in a place of safety.'" Ahmad said: 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd was the first of the Qadaris who denied intercession, so beware of him. The verse does not correspond to the anecdote, but al-Zamakhshari proceeds on the basis that there is no difference between believing in intercession and believing that the unbelievers carry the sins of their followers, so he put the two on a single footing. We seek refuge in God from that. In His words "indeed they are liars" is a fine point from which one may argue for the soundness of a command being used in the sense of a report: for some people denied it and committed themselves to reinterpreting everything transmitted on that matter according to the original sense of command, but this was not complete for them in this verse, because God followed their words "and we will carry your sins," in imperative form, with His words "indeed they are liars," and the charge of lying applies only to reports.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «وبعض المتسمين بالإسلام إذا أراد أن يشجع صاحبه على ذنب قال له: افعل هذا وإثمه في عنقي. ومنه ما يحكى أن رجلا رفع إلى المنصور حوائجه فلما قضاها، قال يا أمير المؤمنين، بقيت لي إليك حاجة هي العظمى. قال: وما هي؟ قال: شفاعتك في المحشر. فقال عمرو: يا أمير المؤمنين، إياك وهؤلاء فهم قطاع الطريق في المأمن» قال أحمد: عمرو بن عبيد أول القدرية المنكرين للشفاعة فاحذره، وليست الآية مطابقة للحكاية، ولكن الزمخشري يبنى على أنه لا فرق بين اعتقاد الشفاعة واعتقاد أن الكفار يحملون خطايا أتباعهم، فلذلك ساقهما مساقا واحدا نعوذ بالله من ذلك. وفي قوله تعالى: إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ نكتة حسنة يستدل بها على صحة مجيء الأمر بمعنى الخبر، فان من الناس من أنكره والتزم تخريج جميع ما ورد في ذلك على أصل الأمر، ولم يتم له ذلك في هذه الآية، لأن الله تعالى أردف قولهم: ولنحمل خطاياكم، على صيغة الأمر بقوله إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ والتكذيب إنما يتطرق إلى الاخبار.
Vol. 3, p. 445
1. (1). Mahmud said: "He turned away from 'nine hundred and fifty' because it admits applying the number to most of it, unlike its coming with the exception." Ahmad said: Because the exception is a rectification and a return upon the whole sentence with a reduction, to make the number exact, so it does not admit exaggeration, since exaggeration does not permit [precise] numbers.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «عدل عن تسعمائة وخمسين لأنه يحتمل فيه إطلاق العدد على أكثره بخلاف مجيئه مع الاستثناء» قال أحمد: لأن الاستثناء استدراك ورجوع على الجملة بالتنقيص، تحريرا للعدد، فلا يحتمل المبالغة لأنها لا يجوز معها العدد.

Q 29:14–15 · Vol. 3, pp. 445–446

Verses 14 to 15

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers (14) So We saved him and the companions of the ship, and We made it a sign for the worlds (15)
وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلاَّ خَمْسِينَ عاماً فَأَخَذَهُمُ الطُّوفانُ وَهُمْ ظالِمُونَ (14) فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَأَصْحابَ السَّفِينَةِ وَجَعَلْناها آيَةً لِلْعالَمِينَ (15)
Vol. 3, p. 445
Noah's age ﷺ was a thousand and fifty years: he was sent at the head of forty, remained among his people nine hundred and fifty, and lived sixty after the flood. And from Wahb: that he lived fourteen hundred years.
كان عمر نوح عليه السلام ألفا وخمسين سنة، بعث على رأس أربعين، ولبث في قومه تسعمائة وخمسين، وعاش بعد الطوفان ستين. وعن وهب: أنه عاش ألفا وأربعمائة سنة.
Question
If you ask: Why was it not said "nine hundred and fifty years"?
فإن قلت: هلا قيل تسعمائة وخمسين سنة؟
Answer
I say: what God set down is wiser. For had it been said as you say, it might have been imagined that the number was applied loosely to most of it; whereas this imagining disappears with its coming as it did, and it is as if it were said: "nine hundred and fifty years, complete and full in number" — except that this [form] is shorter, sweeter in sound and fuller of benefit [1]. And in it is another fine point: the story is told to relate what Noah ﷺ was tried with from his community and what he endured of long patience, as consolation to the Messenger of God ﷺ and to steady him; so mentioning the round number, beyond which there is no larger round number, is more telling and better conveys the purpose, in making the listener feel how long his patience lasted.
قلت: ما أورده الله أحكم. لأنه لو قيل كما قلت، لجاز أن يتوهم إطلاق هذا العدد على أكثره، وهذا التوهم زائل مع مجيئه كذلك، وكأنه قيل: تسعمائة وخمسين سنة كاملة وافية العدد، إلا أنّ ذلك أخصر وأعذب لفظا وأملأ بالفائدة «1» ، وفيه نكتة أخرى: وهي أنّ القصة مسوقة لذكر ما ابتلى به نوح عليه السلام من أمّته وما كابده من طول المصابرة، تسلية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وتثبيتا له، فكان ذكر رأس العدد الذي لا رأس أكثر منه، أوقع وأوصل إلى الغرض من استطالة السامع مدّة صبره.
Question
If you ask: Why did the specified noun come first as "year" and second as "'ām"?
فإن قلت: فلم جاء المميز أوّلا بالسنة وثانيا بالعام؟
Answer
I say: because repeating the same word in the same sentence
قلت: لأنّ تكرير اللفظ الواحد في الكلام الواحد
Vol. 3, p. 446
is to be avoided in rhetoric, unless it occurs for a purpose the speaker aims at, such as magnification, or intimidation [1], or exaltation, or the like. The "ṭūfān" is whatever encircles and surrounds with abundance and overpowering force, whether a torrent, the darkness of night, or the like. Al-'Ajjaj said: "And the flood of darkness covered the athab trees" [2]. "The companions of the ship" were seventy-eight persons: half male and half female, among them the sons of Noah ﷺ: Shem, Ham and Japheth, and their wives. And from Muhammad ibn Ishaq: they were ten: five men and five women. And it is reported from the Prophet ﷺ: "They were eight: Noah, his family, and his three sons" [3]. The pronoun in "and We made it" refers to the ship, or to the event and the story.
حقيق بالاجتناب في البلاغة، إلا إذا وقع ذلك لأجل غرض ينتحيه المتكلم من تفخيم أو تهويل «1» أو تنويه أو نحو ذلك. والطُّوفانُ ما أطاف وأحاط بكثرة وغلبة، من سيل أو ظلام ليل أو نحوهما. قال العجاج: وغمّ طوفان الظّلام الأثأبا «2» أَصْحابَ السَّفِينَةِ كانوا ثمانية وسبعين نفسا: نصفهم ذكور، ونصفهم إناث، منهم أولاد نوح عليه السلام: سام، وحام، ويافث، ونساؤهم. وعن محمد بن إسحاق: كانوا عشرة. خمسة رجال وخمس نسوة. وقد روى عن النبىّ صلى الله عليه وسلم «كانوا ثمانية: نوح وأهله وبنوه الثلاثة» «3» والضمير في وَجَعَلْناها للسفينة أو للحادثة والقصة.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 3, p. 445
1. (1). Mahmud said: "He turned away from 'nine hundred and fifty' because it admits applying the number to most of it, unlike its coming with the exception." Ahmad said: Because the exception is a rectification and a return upon the whole sentence with a reduction, to make the number exact, so it does not admit exaggeration, since exaggeration does not permit [precise] numbers.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «عدل عن تسعمائة وخمسين لأنه يحتمل فيه إطلاق العدد على أكثره بخلاف مجيئه مع الاستثناء» قال أحمد: لأن الاستثناء استدراك ورجوع على الجملة بالتنقيص، تحريرا للعدد، فلا يحتمل المبالغة لأنها لا يجوز معها العدد.
Vol. 3, p. 446
1. (1). His discourse resumed. He said: "And in it is another fine point, namely that the story is told to relate what Noah was tried with and endured of long patience, as consolation to him ﷺ so mentioning the round number beyond which there is no larger better serves the purpose. He said: He varied between the two expressions, mentioning 'year' in the first and 'year ('ām)' in the second, avoiding repetition, which is not praiseworthy except for the purpose of magnification or glorification." Ahmad said: But if the thing excepted were magnified, that would return as some magnification and enlargement of the thing excepted from, in the listener's mind. And God knows best.
2. "Until when its day began to pour... and the flood of darkness covered the athab trees," by al-'Ajjaj, describing a wild cow. "Mā" is redundant. It is transmitted "'amma" with the undotted 'ayn and with the dotted ghayn ["ghamma"], and the two meanings are close. "Al-ṭūfān" is everything that circles around a thing and surrounds it of darkness, water or the like. "Al-athab" is a kind of tree resembling the fig tree, the singular being "athaba." The ascription of pouring to "today" [here "its day"] is a rational figure of speech of the type of ascribing to time, or it is on the basis of specification, i.e. it poured rain, and its darkness covered the trees in which it was.
3. This preceded in [Surat] Hud.
1. (1) . عاد كلامه. قال: «وفيه نكتة أخرى، وهي أن القصة مسوقة لذكر ما ابتلى به نوح وكابده من طول المصابرة، تسلية له عليه السلام فكان ذكر رأس العدد الذي لا رأس أكثر منه أوقع على الغرض. قال: وإنما خالف بين اللفظين فذكر في الأول السنة وفي الثاني العام، تجنبا للتكرار الذي لا يحمد إلا لقصد تفخيم أو تعظيم» قال أحمد: ولو فخم المستثنى لعاد ذلك ببعض تفخيم المستثنى منه وتكبيره عند السامع، والله أعلم.
2. . حتى إذا ما يومها تصيبا
…. وعم طوفان الظلام الأثأبا للعجاج يصف بقرة وحشية. وما: زائدة. ويروى: عم، بالمهملة وبالمعجمة، والمعنيان متقاربان. والطوفان: كل ما طاف حول الشيء وأحاط به من ظلام أو ماء أو نحوهما. والأثأب: نوع من الشجر يشبه شجر التين، الواحدة: أثأبة ونسبة التصبب اليوم: مجاز عقلى من باب الاسناد للزمان، أو على تقدير التمييز، أى: تصبب مطرا، وستر ظلامه الشجر الذي كانت فيه.
3. . تقدم في هود.
12
Q 29:16–18 · Vol. 3, pp. 446–447

Verses 16 to 18

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And Abraham, when he said to his people, "Worship God and fear Him; that is better for you, if you only knew (16) You only worship, instead of God, idols, and you fabricate falsehood. Indeed those you worship besides God do not possess for you any provision; so seek provision from God, and worship Him and be grateful to Him; to Him you will be returned (17) And if you deny, then nations before you have denied; and the Messenger is only responsible for clear delivery (18)
وَإِبْراهِيمَ إِذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاتَّقُوهُ ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (16) إِنَّما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْثاناً وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكاً إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لا يَمْلِكُونَ لَكُمْ رِزْقاً فَابْتَغُوا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الرِّزْقَ وَاعْبُدُوهُ وَاشْكُرُوا لَهُ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ (17) وَإِنْ تُكَذِّبُوا فَقَدْ كَذَّبَ أُمَمٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَما عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلاَّ الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ (18)
Vol. 3, p. 446
"Abraham" is accusative by an implied "remember," and "when" is substituted for it as an inclusive substitution, since times include what is in them. Or it is coordinated with "Noah," and "when" is a time-adverb of "We sent," meaning: We sent him when he had reached an age and knowledge in which he was fit to exhort his people, advise them, present the truth to them, and command them to worship and God-fearing
نصب إِبْراهِيمَ بإضمار اذكر، وأبدل عنه إِذْ بدل الاشتمال، لأنّ الأحيان تشتمل على ما فيها. أو هو معطوف على نُوحاً وإذ ظرف لأرسلنا، يعنى: أرسلناه حين بلغ من السنّ والعلم مبلغا صلح فيه لأن يعظ قومه وينصحهم ويعرض عليهم الحق ويأمرهم بالعبادة والتقوى
Vol. 3, p. 447
Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Abu Hanifa ؒ both) read "wa-Ibrāhīmu" in the nominative, meaning: "and among the messengers was Abraham." "If you only knew" means: if you had knowledge of what is better for you as against what is worse for you; or: if you looked with the eye of seeing insight rather than the blind eye of ignorance, you would know that it is better for you. It is also read "takhalluqūna" from "khallaqa" in the sense of intensification of "khalaqa," and "takhalaqūna" from "takhallaqa" in the sense of lying and conjecturing. It is also read "ifkan," which has two aspects: that it is a verbal noun like "kadhib" and "la'ib," and "ifk" is a lightened form of it, as "kadhb" and "la'b" from their originals; and that it is an adjective on the pattern fa'ul, i.e. "a false creation," i.e. possessing falsehood and vanity. Their fabricating falsehood is: their calling the idols gods and partners of God or intercessors with Him; or He called the idols "falsehood," and their making and carving of them "creating of falsehood."
وقرأ إبراهيم النخعي وأبو حنيفة رحمهما الله. وإبراهيم، بالرفع على معنى: ومن المرسلين إبراهيم إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ يعنى: إن كان فيكم علم بما هو خير لكم مما هو شر لكم. أو إن نظرتم بعين الدراية المبصرة دون عين الجهل العمياء: علمتم أنه خير لكم: وقرئ: تخلقون من خلق بمعنى التكثير في خلق. وتخلقون، من تخلق بمعنى تكذب وتخرص. وقرئ: إفكا، فيه وجهان: أن يكون مصدرا، نحو: كذب ولعب. والإفك: مخفف منه، كالكذب واللعب من أصلهما، وأن يكون صفة على فعل، أى خلقا إفكا، أى ذا إفك وباطل. واختلاقهم الإفك: تسميتهم الأوثان آلهة وشركاء لله أو شفعاء إليه. أو سمى الأصنام: إفكا، وعملهم لها ونحتهم: خلقا للإفك.
Question
If you ask: Why was "provision" made indefinite, then definite?
فإن قلت: لم نكر الرزق ثم عرفه؟
Answer
I say: because He meant: they are unable to provide you any provision at all, so "seek the provision" in its entirety from God, for He alone is the Provider and provides no other. "To Him you will be returned" — it is also read with fatḥa on the tā' ["turja'ūn," you return] — so prepare for meeting Him by worshiping Him and giving thanks to Him for His favors; "and if you deny me," you do not harm me by your denial, for the messengers before me were denied by their nations, and they did not harm them, but only harmed themselves, when what befell them befell them because of denying the messengers; as for the messenger, his task is complete when he has delivered "the clear delivery" by which doubt is removed, namely its being accompanied by God's signs and miracles. Or: if you are denying among yourselves, I have in the other prophets a model and consolation, since they were denied; and it is for the messenger to deliver, not to make [people] believe or disbelieve. This verse and those after it up to His words "So the answer of his people was only" may be part of Abraham's (God's blessings upon him) speech to his people, or may be verses inserted parenthetically concerning the Messenger of God ﷺ and Quraysh, between the beginning of the story of Abraham and its end.
قلت: لأنه أراد لا يستطيعون أن يرزقوكم شيئا من الرزق، فابتغوا عند الله الرزق كله. فإنه هو الرزاق وحده لا يرزق غيره إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ وقرئ: بفتح التاء، فاستعدوا للقائه بعبادته والشكر له على أنعمه، وإن تكذبونني فلا تضروننى بتكذيبكم، فإنّ الرسل قبلي قد كذبتهم أممهم، وما ضرّوهم وإنما ضروا أنفسهم، حيث حلّ بهم ما حل بسبب تكذيب الرسل: وأما الرسول فقد تم أمره حين بلغ البلاغ المبين الذي زال معه الشكّ، وهو اقترانه بآيات الله ومعجزاته. أو: وإن كنت مكذبا فيما بينكم فلي في سائر الأنبياء أسوة وسلوة حيث كذبوا، وعلى الرسول أن يبلغ وما عليه أن يصدق ولا يكذب، وهذه الآية والآيات التي بعدها إلى قوله فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ محتملة أن تكون من جملة قول إبراهيم صلوات الله عليه لقومه، وأن تكون آيات وقعت معترضة في شأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وشأن قريش بين أوّل قصة إبراهيم وآخرها.
Question
If you ask: If they are from Abraham's speech, what is meant by the nations before him?
فإن قلت: إذا كانت من قول إبراهيم فما المراد بالأمم قبله؟
Answer
I say: the people of Seth and Idris and Noah and others; and the people of Noah suffice as a nation equivalent to many denying nations. And Idris lived a thousand years among his people until he was raised to heaven, and a thousand people of them believed in him, equal to the number of his years, while their descendants [remained] in denial.
قلت: قوم شيث وإدريس ونوح وغيرهم، وكفى بقوم نوح أمّة في معنى أمم جمة مكذبة، ولقد عاش إدريس ألف سنة في قومه إلى أن رفع إلى السماء. وآمن به ألف إنسان منهم على عدد سنيه، وأعقابهم على التكذيب.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 446

He said: "And in it is another fine point, namely that the story is told to relate what Noah was tried with and endured of long patience, as consolation to him ﷺ so mentioning the round number beyond which there is no larger better serves the purpose. He said: He varied between the two expressions, mentioning 'year' in the first and 'year ('ām)' in the second, avoiding repetition, which is not praiseworthy except for the purpose of magnification or glorification." Ahmad said: But if the thing excepted were magnified, that would return as some magnification and enlargement of the thing excepted from, in the listener's mind. And God knows best.
2. "Until when its day began to pour... and the flood of darkness covered the athab trees," by al-'Ajjaj, describing a wild cow. "Mā" is redundant. It is transmitted "'amma" with the undotted 'ayn and with the dotted ghayn ["ghamma"], and the two meanings are close. "Al-ṭūfān" is everything that circles around a thing and surrounds it of darkness, water or the like. "Al-athab" is a kind of tree resembling the fig tree, the singular being "athaba." The ascription of pouring to "today" [here "its day"] is a rational figure of speech of the type of ascribing to time, or it is on the basis of specification, i.e. it poured rain, and its darkness covered the trees in which it was.
3. This preceded in [Surat] Hud.
1. (1) . عاد كلامه. قال: «وفيه نكتة أخرى، وهي أن القصة مسوقة لذكر ما ابتلى به نوح وكابده من طول المصابرة، تسلية له عليه السلام فكان ذكر رأس العدد الذي لا رأس أكثر منه أوقع على الغرض. قال: وإنما خالف بين اللفظين فذكر في الأول السنة وفي الثاني العام، تجنبا للتكرار الذي لا يحمد إلا لقصد تفخيم أو تعظيم» قال أحمد: ولو فخم المستثنى لعاد ذلك ببعض تفخيم المستثنى منه وتكبيره عند السامع، والله أعلم.
2. . حتى إذا ما يومها تصيبا
…. وعم طوفان الظلام الأثأبا للعجاج يصف بقرة وحشية. وما: زائدة. ويروى: عم، بالمهملة وبالمعجمة، والمعنيان متقاربان. والطوفان: كل ما طاف حول الشيء وأحاط به من ظلام أو ماء أو نحوهما. والأثأب: نوع من الشجر يشبه شجر التين، الواحدة: أثأبة ونسبة التصبب اليوم: مجاز عقلى من باب الاسناد للزمان، أو على تقدير التمييز، أى: تصبب مطرا، وستر ظلامه الشجر الذي كانت فيه.
3. . تقدم في هود.

Q 29:19–22 · Vol. 3, pp. 447–449

Verses 19 to 22

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Have they not seen how God originates creation, then repeats it? Indeed that is easy for God (19) Say, "Travel through the earth and see how He began creation; then God will produce the final creation. Indeed God is over all things competent (20) He punishes whom He wills and has mercy upon whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned (21) And you will not be able to escape [Him] on earth or in the heaven, and you have not besides God any ally or helper (22)
أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَيْفَ يُبْدِئُ اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ إِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ (19) قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنْشِئُ النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (20) يُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَرْحَمُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَإِلَيْهِ تُقْلَبُونَ (21) وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي السَّماءِ وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلا نَصِيرٍ (22)
Vol. 3, p. 448
If you ask: Then what do you do with His words "Say, 'Travel through the earth'"? I say: it is the report of speech that Abraham ﷺ related to his people, just as our Messenger ﷺ relates the speech of God in this manner in most of the Qur'an. If you ask: But if it is addressed to Quraysh, what is the reason for placing the two verses between the two ends of Abraham's story and the sentence? Must parenthetical sentences not have a connection to what they are inserted into? Do you not see that you cannot say: "Mecca — and Zayd his father is standing — is the best of God's lands"? I say: the mention of Abraham's story is only meant to relieve the Messenger of God ﷺ and to be a consolation and relief to him, that his father Abraham, the Friend of God, was afflicted [1] with the like of what he was afflicted with of his people's polytheism and their worship of idols; so He inserted the saying "And if you deny," meaning: "O people of Quraysh, if you deny Muhammad, Abraham denied his people too, and every nation its prophet," because His words "then nations before you have denied" must include Abraham's nation; and it is, as you see, a parenthesis that falls in a connected position [2]; then the remaining verses that follow it are its appendages and adjuncts, because they speak of divine oneness and its proofs, the demolition of polytheism and weakening of its foundations, the description of God's power and authority, and the clarity of His argument and proof. "Yaraw" is read with yā' and tā'. "Yubdi'u" and "yubda'u" [are both read]. And His words "then repeats it" are not coordinated with "originates," and the seeing does not fall upon it; rather it is a report in itself of the repetition after death, just as the looking falls in His words "see how He began creation; then God will produce the final creation" on the beginning rather than the producing; its like is your saying: "I continue to prefer so-and-so and appoint him successor over those I leave behind" [3]. If you ask: It is coordinated with a conjunction, so it must have something coordinated to; what is it? I say: it is the sentence of His words "Have they not seen how God originates creation," and likewise "and appoint him successor" is coordinated to the sentence "I continue to prefer so-and-so." "That" refers to what "it" refers to in His words "and it is easier for Him," of the meaning of "repeats." By "the final creation" He indicated that there are two creations and that each of them is a producing, i.e. a beginning and invention, a bringing out from non-existence into existence, with no difference between them except that the last is a producing after a producing like it, while the first is not so. It is also read "al-nash'a" and "al-nashā'a," like "al-ra'fa" and "al-ra'āfa." If you ask: What is the meaning of stating His name explicitly while making it a subject in His words "then God will produce the final creation," after having used a pronoun in "how He began creation"?
فإن قلت: فما تصنع بقوله قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ؟ قلت: هي حكاية كلام حكاه إبراهيم عليه السلام لقومه، كما يحكى رسولنا صلى الله عليه وسلم كلام الله على هذا المنهاج في أكثر القرآن فإن قلت: فإذا كانت خطابا لقريش فما وجه توسطهما بين طرفى قصة إبراهيم والجملة؟ أو الجمل الاعتراضية لا بد لها من اتصال بما وقعت معترضة فيه؟ ألا تراك لا تقول: مكة- وزيد أبوه قائم- خير بلاد الله؟ قلت: إيراد قصة إبراهيم ليس إلا إرادة للتنفيس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأن تكون مسلاة له ومتفرجا بأنّ أباه إبراهيم خليل الله كان ممنوّا بنحو ما مني «1» به من شرك قومه وعبادتهم الأوثان، فاعترض بقوله: وإن تكذبوا، على معنى إنكم يا معشر قريش إن تكذبوا محمدا فقد كذب إبراهيم قومه وكل أمة نبيها، لأن قوله فَقَدْ كَذَّبَ أُمَمٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ لا بد من تناوله لأمّة إبراهيم، وهو كما ترى اعتراض واقع «2» متصل، ثم سائر الآيات الواطئة عقبها من أذيالها وتوابعها، لكونها ناطقة بالتوحيد ودلائله، وهدم الشرك وتوهين قواعده، وصفة قدرة الله وسلطانه، ووضوح حجته وبرهانه. قرئ يَرَوْا بالياء والتاء. ويبدئ ويبدأ. وقوله ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ليس بمعطوف على يبدئ، وليست الرؤية واقعة عليه، وإنما هو إخبار على حياله بالإعادة بعد الموت، كما وقع النظر في قوله تعالى: فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنْشِئُ النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ على البدء دون الإنشاء، ونحوه قولك: ما زلت أوثر فلانا وأستخلفه على من أخلفه «3» . فإن قلت: هو معطوف بحرف العطف، فلا بد له من معطوف عليه، فما هو؟ قلت: هو جملة قوله أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَيْفَ يُبْدِئُ اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ وكذلك: وأستخلفه، معطوف على جملة قوله: ما زلت أوثر فلانا ذلِكَ يرجع إلى ما يرجع إليه هو في قوله وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ من معنى يعيد. دل بقوله النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ على أنهما نشأتان، وأن كل واحدة منهما إنشاء، أى: ابتداء واختراع، وإخراج من العدم إلى الوجود، لا تفاوت بينهما إلا أن الآخرة إنشاء بعد إنشاء مثله، والأولى ليست كذلك. وقرئ: النشأة والنشاءة، كالرأفة والرآفة. فإن قلت: ما معنى الإفصاح باسمه مع إيقاعه مبتدأ في قوله ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنْشِئُ النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ بعد إضماره في قوله: كيف بدأ الخلق؟
Vol. 3, p. 449
Surely the analogy would be to say: "see how God began creation; then He will produce the final creation"? I say: the discourse with them was about the repetition, and it was over it that their knees knocked; so when He had them acknowledge, regarding the beginning, that it is from God, He argued against them that the repetition is a producing like the beginning, so if God, whom nothing can overcome, is the One whom the beginning did not overcome, then He is the One whom the repetition must not overcome [1]; it is as if He said: "then that One who produced the first creation is the One who will produce the last creation"; so, to indicate and alert to this meaning, He brought out His name and made it a subject. "He punishes whom He wills" — His punishing him — "and has mercy upon whom He wills" — His mercy on him; and the object of the two wills is explained and clarified in places in the Qur'an [2], and it is whoever deserves them, of the unbeliever and the sinner if they do not repent, and the protected and the repentant. "You will be returned" means you will be brought back and sent back. "And you will not be able to escape" your Lord, i.e. you cannot elude Him if you flee from His judgment and decree, "on the earth," the spacious, "or in the heaven," which is more spacious and wider than it, if you were in it, as in His words: "If you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass." And it is said: "nor [will] those in the heaven" [3], as Hassan ؓ said: "Is he who satirizes the Messenger of God among you, and he who praises him and helps him, the same?" [4] It may also be meant: you cannot defeat Him however you descend into the pits and depths of the earth, or rise in the towers and fortresses reaching toward the sky, as in His words "even if you were in lofty towers." Or: you cannot frustrate His command that runs in heaven and earth from coming upon you, so that it strikes you with a calamity that appears from the earth or descends from heaven.
وكان القياس أن يقال: كيف بدأ الله الخلق ثم ينشئ النشأة الآخرة؟ قلت: الكلام معهم كان واقعا في الإعادة، وفيها كانت تصطك الركب، فلما قرّرهم في الإبداء بأنه من الله، احتج عليهم بأن الإعادة إنشاء مثل الإبداء، فإذا كان الله الذي لا يعجزه شيء هو الذي لم يعجزه الإبداء، فهو الذي وجب أن لا تعجزه الإعادة «1» ، فكأنه قال: ثم ذاك الذي أنشأ النشأة الأولى هو الذي ينشئ النشأة الآخرة، فللدلالة والتنبيه على هذا المعنى أبرز اسمه وأوقعه مبتدأ يُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ تعذيبه وَيَرْحَمُ مَنْ يَشاءُ رحمته، ومتعلق المشيئتين مفسر مبين في مواضع من القرآن «2» وهو من يستوجبهما من الكافر والفاسق إذا لم يتوبا، ومن المعصوم والتائب تُقْلَبُونَ تردون وترجعون وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ ربكم أى لا تفوتونه إن هربتم من حكمه وقضائه فِي الْأَرْضِ الفسيحة وَلا فِي السَّماءِ التي هي أفسح منها وأبسط لو كنتم فيها، كقوله تعالى: إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَنْفُذُوا مِنْ أَقْطارِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانْفُذُوا، وقيل: ولا من في السماء «3» كما قال حسان رضى الله عنه: أمن يهجو رسول الله منكم … ويمدحه وينصره سواء «4» ويحتمل أن يراد: لا تعجزونه كيفما هبطتم في مهاوي الأرض وأعماقها، أو علوتم في البروج والقلاع الذاهبة في السماء، كقوله تعالى وَلَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُرُوجٍ مُشَيَّدَةٍ أو لا تعجزون أمره الجاري في السماء والأرض أن يجرى عليكم، فيصيبكم ببلاء يظهر من الأرض أو ينزل من السماء.

1. (1) . قوله «كان ممنوا بنحو ماضى؟؟؟ به» أى: مبتلى. في الصحاح: منوته ومنيته، إذا ابتليته. (ع)
2. . قوله «وهو كما ترى اعتراض واقع» لعله: واقع موقعه. (ع)
3. . قال محمود: «يعيده ليس معطوفا على يبدئ، وإنما هو إخبار على حياله، كما وقع كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنْشِئُ النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ كقولك ما زلت أوثر فلانا وأستخلفه بعدي» قال أحمد، وقد تقدم له عند قوله تعالى أَمَّنْ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ أنه معطوف، وصحح العطف- وإن كانوا ينكرون الاعادة- لأن الاعتراف بها لازم لهم، وقد أبى هاهنا جعله معطوفا، فالفرق والله أعلم أنه هاهنا لو عطف الاعادة على البداءة لدخلت في الرؤية الماضية، وهي لم تقع بعد، ولا كذلك في آية النمل، ولقائل أن يقول: هي وإن لم تقع، إلا أنها باخبار الله تعالى بوقوعها كالواقعة المرئية، فعوملت معاملة ما رئي وشوهد إلا أن جعله خبرا ثانيا أوضح، والله أعلم.

(1) . قال محمود: «إن قلت ما وجه الإفصاح باسمه تعالى مع النشأة الآخرة، بعد إضماره في البداءة أو لا؟ قلت: لأن النشأة الآخرة هي المقصودة وفيها كانت تصطك الركب، فكانت خليقة بإبراز اسمه تعالى تحقيقا لنسبة الاعادة إلى من نسبت إليه الأولى» قال أحمد: والأصل الاظهار ثم الإضمار، ويليه لقصد التفخيم: الاظهار بعد الاظهار، ويليه وهو أفخم الثلاثة: الاظهار بعد الإضمار كما في الآية، والله أعلم.
2. . قوله «ومتعلق المشيئتين مفسر مبين في مواضع من القرآن» تفسيره بما يأتى مبنى على أنه تعالى يجب عليه تعذيب الكافر والفاسق إذا لم يتوبا وإثابة المعصوم والتائب، وهو مذهب المعتزلة. ولا يجب عليه تعالى شيء عند أهل السنة، فالمشيئة في الآية على إطلاقها. (ع) [.....]
3. . قوله «وقيل ولا من في السماء» عبارة الخازن: ولا من في السماء بمعجز. (ع)

Q 29:23 · Vol. 3, pp. 449–450

Verse 23

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And those who disbelieve in the signs of God and in meeting Him, those have despaired of My mercy, and those will have a painful punishment (23)
وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ وَلِقائِهِ أُولئِكَ يَئِسُوا مِنْ رَحْمَتِي وَأُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ (23)
Vol. 3, p. 449
"In the signs of God," i.e. His proofs of His oneness, His books and miracles, "and in meeting Him," and the resurrection. "Have despaired of My mercy" is a threat, i.e. they will despair on the Day of Resurrection, as in His words: "And on the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will be in despair." Or it is a description
بِآياتِ اللَّهِ بدلائله على وحدانيته وكتبه ومعجزاته ولقائه والبعث يَئِسُوا مِنْ رَحْمَتِي وعيد، أى ييأسون يوم القيامة، كقوله: وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يُبْلِسُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ. أو هو وصف
Vol. 3, p. 450
of their state, because the believer is only ever hopeful and fearful, whereas the unbeliever has neither hope nor fear cross his mind. Or it likens their state in having mercy removed from them to the state of one who despairs of mercy. And from Qatada ؓ: God censured a people who were of no worth to Him, saying "those have despaired of My mercy," and said: "Indeed no one despairs of the mercy of God except the disbelieving people." So the believer should neither despair of God's relief and mercy nor feel secure from His punishment and chastisement; [for] it is the attribute of the believer [1] to be hopeful of God, the Mighty and Majestic, and fearful.
لحالهم، لأنّ المؤمن إنما يكون راجيا خاشيا، فأما الكافر فلا يخطر بباله رجاء ولا خوف. أو شبه حالهم في انتفاء الرحمة عنهم بحال من يئس من الرحمة: وعن قتادة رضى الله عنه. إن الله ذمّ قوما هانوا عليه فقال أُولئِكَ يَئِسُوا مِنْ رَحْمَتِي وقال إِنَّهُ لا يَيْأَسُ مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْكافِرُونَ فينبغي للمؤمن أن لا ييأس من روح الله ولا من رحمته، وأن لا يأمن عذابه وعقابه صفة المؤمن «1» أن يكون راجيا لله عز وجل خائفا.

Q 29:24 · Vol. 3, p. 450

Verse 24

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And the answer of his people was not but that they said, "Kill him or burn him"; but God saved him from the fire. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe (24)
فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلاَّ أَنْ قالُوا اقْتُلُوهُ أَوْ حَرِّقُوهُ فَأَنْجاهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ النَّارِ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ (24)
Vol. 3, p. 450
"The answer of his people" is read in the accusative and the nominative. "They said" means some said to others; or one of them said it and the rest were content, so they were all in the ruling of speakers. It is reported that on that day the fire gave no benefit — meaning the day Abraham was thrown into the fire — because its heat departed.
قرئ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ بالنصب والرفع قالُوا قال بعضهم لبعض. أو قاله واحد منهم وكان الباقون راضين، فكانوا جميعا في حكم القائلين. وروى أنه لم ينتفع في ذلك اليوم بالنار، نعنى: يوم ألقى إبراهيم في النار، وذلك لذهاب حرّها.

Q 29:25 · Vol. 3, pp. 450–451

Verse 25

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And he said, "You have only taken, besides God, idols as a bond of affection among you in worldly life. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will deny one another and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers" (25)
وَقالَ إِنَّمَا اتَّخَذْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْثاناً مَوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا ثُمَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يَكْفُرُ بَعْضُكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ وَيَلْعَنُ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضاً وَمَأْواكُمُ النَّارُ وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ ناصِرِينَ (25)
Vol. 3, p. 450
It is read in the accusative without annexation and with annexation, and in the nominative likewise. The accusative has two aspects: as a reason, i.e. "so that you may love one another and keep close to one another because you gather around worshiping them, agree on them and are united," as people agree on a doctrine and that becomes the cause of their mutual love and friendship; and that it is a second object, as in "he has taken his desire as his god," i.e. "you have taken the idols as the cause of affection among you," with the annexed word omitted; or "you have taken them as an affection among you," meaning "beloved among you," as in His words: "And among the people are those who take, besides God, equals; they love them as they love God." In the nominative there are two aspects: that it is the predicate of "inna," with "mā" a relative pronoun; and that it is the predicate of an omitted subject. The meaning is that the idols are an affection among you, i.e. beloved, or the cause of affection. And from 'Asim: "mawaddata baynikum" with fatḥa on "baynikum" together with annexation, as "Your ties have been severed (taqaṭṭa'a baynukum)" is read with fatḥa, and it is the subject. And Ibn Mas'ud ؓ read: "awthānan innamā mawaddatu baynikum fī'l-ḥayāti'l-dunyā," i.e. "you only love one another over them" or "you love them in worldly life." "Then on the Day of Resurrection" there will arise among you mutual cursing
قرئ على النصب بغير إضافة وبإضافة، وعلى الرفع كذلك، فالنصب على وجهين: على التعليل، أى لتتوادّوا بينكم وتتواصلوا، لاجتماعكم على عبادتها واتفاقكم عليها وائتلافكم، كما يتفق الناس على مذهب فيكون ذلك سبب تحابهم وتصادقهم. وأن يكون مفعولا ثانيا، كقوله اتَّخَذَ إِلهَهُ هَواهُ أى اتخذتم الأوثان سبب المودّة بينكم، على تقدير حذف المضاف. أو اتخذتموها مودّة بينكم، بمعنى مودودة بينكم، كقوله تعالى وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْداداً يُحِبُّونَهُمْ كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ وفي الرفع وجهان: أن يكون خبرا لأنّ، على أن ما موصولة. وأن يكون خبر مبتدإ محذوف. والمعنى: أنّ الأوثان مودّة بينكم، أى: مودودة، أو سبب مودّة. وعن عاصم: مودّة بينكم: بفتح بينكم مع الإضافة، كما قرئ لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ ففتح وهو فاعل. وقرأ ابن مسعود رضى الله عنه: أوثانا إنما مودّة بينكم في الحياة الدنيا، أى: إنما تتوادّون عليها، أو تودّونها في الحياة الدنيا ثُمَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يقوم بينكم التلاعن
Vol. 3, p. 451
and hatred and enmity: the worshipers will curse one another, and the worshipers and the idols will curse one another, as in His words "and they will be against them an opposition."
والتباغض والتعادي: يتلاعن العبدة، ويتلاعن العبدة والأصنام، كقوله تعالى وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدًّا.
